title: Apple (AAPL) Insider Luca Maestri Sells 4,769 Shares of Stock
text:
Tweet
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) insider Luca Maestri sold 4,769 shares of the firm’s stock in a transaction that occurred on Friday, June 1st. The stock was sold at an average price of $189.54, for a total transaction of $903,916.26. Following the sale, the insider now directly owns 68,044 shares in the company, valued at approximately $12,897,059.76. The transaction was disclosed in a document filed with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which is available at this link .
Luca Maestri also recently made the following trade(s): Get Apple alerts: On Friday, April 13th, Luca Maestri sold 39,122 shares of Apple stock. The stock was sold at an average price of $174.66, for a total transaction of $6,833,048.52.
Shares of Apple opened at $191.83 on Tuesday, Marketbeat Ratings reports. Apple has a twelve month low of $142.20 and a twelve month high of $193.42. The stock has a market capitalization of $965.28 billion, a P/E ratio of 20.83, a PEG ratio of 1.41 and a beta of 1.29. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.80, a current ratio of 1.46 and a quick ratio of 1.37. Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last announced its earnings results on Tuesday, May 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.73 earnings per share for the quarter, beating the consensus estimate of $2.69 by $0.04. Apple had a net margin of 21.55% and a return on equity of 39.97%. The firm had revenue of $61.14 billion during the quarter, compared to the consensus estimate of $60.94 billion. During the same quarter in the previous year, the company posted $2.10 EPS. The firm’s revenue for the quarter was up 15.6% on a year-over-year basis. analysts expect that Apple will post 11.43 EPS for the current year.
Apple declared that its Board of Directors has authorized a stock repurchase plan on Tuesday, May 1st that permits the company to repurchase $100.00 billion in shares. This repurchase authorization permits the iPhone maker to buy up to 11.9% of its shares through open market purchases. Shares repurchase plans are often a sign that the company’s management believes its stock is undervalued.
The company also recently announced a quarterly dividend, which was paid on Thursday, May 17th. Investors of record on Monday, May 14th were paid a $0.73 dividend. This is an increase from Apple’s previous quarterly dividend of $0.63. The ex-dividend date of this dividend was Friday, May 11th. This represents a $2.92 annualized dividend and a yield of 1.52%. Apple’s payout ratio is presently 31.70%.
A number of hedge funds have recently made changes to their positions in AAPL. Jarislowsky Fraser Ltd increased its stake in shares of Apple by 22.4% during the 3rd quarter. Jarislowsky Fraser Ltd now owns 22,515 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $3,470,000 after acquiring an additional 4,118 shares during the last quarter. Fjarde AP Fonden Fourth Swedish National Pension Fund increased its stake in shares of Apple by 1.7% during the 3rd quarter. Fjarde AP Fonden Fourth Swedish National Pension Fund now owns 1,234,364 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $190,240,000 after acquiring an additional 20,689 shares during the last quarter. Shelton Capital Management increased its stake in shares of Apple by 2.3% during the 3rd quarter. Shelton Capital Management now owns 437,397 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $67,412,000 after acquiring an additional 9,758 shares during the last quarter. Hikari Power Ltd acquired a new position in shares of Apple during the 3rd quarter valued at about $208,000. Finally, Oakmont Partners LLC increased its stake in shares of Apple by 10.6% during the 4th quarter. Oakmont Partners LLC now owns 13,971 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $2,364,000 after acquiring an additional 1,335 shares during the last quarter. 58.14% of the stock is owned by hedge funds and other institutional investors.
A number of research firms have weighed in on AAPL. BidaskClub raised shares of Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating in a report on Tuesday, May 29th. Morgan Stanley reissued an “overweight” rating and set a $214.00 price objective (up previously from $200.00) on shares of Apple in a report on Thursday, May 24th. They noted that the move was a valuation call. Maxim Group cut shares of Apple from a “buy” rating to a “hold” rating and cut their price objective for the stock from $204.00 to $200.00 in a report on Wednesday, May 30th. UBS Group lifted their target price on shares of Apple from $190.00 to $210.00 and gave the company a “buy” rating in a report on Friday. Finally, Vetr cut shares of Apple from a “buy” rating to a “hold” rating and set a $184.49 target price on the stock. in a report on Tuesday, February 27th. One equities research analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, sixteen have issued a hold rating, thirty-two have assigned a buy rating and two have issued a strong buy rating to the company. The company currently has an average rating of “Buy” and an average price target of $205.39.
